body: Chosen: for hosts listed as identity providers (preset accounts.google.com, *.google.com, accounts.youtube.com, *.gstatic.com; user-editable) the persona tab neither strips nor sets cookies, so the provider runs in the browser's real jar and the app's own session cookie stays per persona. WHY: Google sets its flow cookie (__Host-GAPS) on a 302 and expects it back on the redirect follow-up; under MV3 only a blocking interception could carry a redirect-set cookie onto that follow-up, and the DNR rule install (measured 1-23 ms) lands after the follow-up has left, 0/10 in the probe. Device Bound Session Credentials refreshes run browser-side, so no per-tab rule can rewrite them. Rejected: (1) cookie swapping, it leaks persona cookies into plain tabs and the browser's login into the persona tab, leaves cookies behind because chrome.cookies.getAll returns [], and forbids two active persona tabs of one site; (2) debugger as a barrier (DNR plus chrome.debugger holding the follow-up until the rule is in), dead because Chrome fixes the DNR header changes before the DevTools Fetch pause, 0/10. Trade-off to surface in the UI: the Google login is shared with the browser. Revisit when per-persona Google accounts become a real need (see the strict sign-in suggestion). Research: docsi/research/google-signin.md
title: Google sign-in in a persona: pass-through identity-provider hosts
